content: 1. Krakauer and Rigodon conducted a study in Malawi to evaluate and address the palliative care needs in rural sub-Saharan Africa. Their findings were based on a model intervention and situational analysis, published in PLOS One. 2. Gott et al. explored the perspectives of healthcare staff in England and New Zealand regarding the role and scope of palliative care. Their study emphasized that palliative care is considered an integral part of every healthcare professional's responsibilities, as published in Palliative Medicine. 3. Higginson and Sen-Gupta examined the preferred place of care for patients with advanced cancer, highlighting the importance of patient-centered care in palliative settings, as detailed in the Journal of Palliative Medicine. 4. The World Health Organization (WHO) Expert Committee on Cancer Pain Relief and Palliative Care published a technical report in 1990, emphasizing the need for effective pain management and palliative care strategies globally. 5. Kumar discussed the community-based palliative care model in Kerala, India, in an interview with Nisha Krishnadas. This model has been recognized for its innovative approach to delivering end-of-life care, as featured in ehospice. 6. Quill and Abernathy proposed a sustainable model combining generalist and specialist palliative care to improve access and efficiency, as published in the New England Journal of Medicine. 7. 8. Shepperd et al. reviewed the concept of hospital at home for end-of-life care, demonstrating its potential to provide effective home-based palliative care, as detailed in the Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. 9. Williams et al. analyzed the varying impacts of caregiving across three groups in Canada: end-of-life care, long-term care, and short-term care. Their findings highlighted the unique challenges faced by caregivers in each category, as published in Health and Social Care in the Community. 10. Brumley et al. conducted a randomized trial on in-home palliative care, showing increased patient satisfaction and reduced costs, as reported in the Journal of the American Geriatrics Society. 11. Grande et al. investigated the relationship between caregiver bereavement outcomes, satisfaction with care, and the occurrence of home deaths. Their study emphasized the importance of quality palliative care in supporting caregivers, as published in the Journal of Palliative Care. 12. Randall and Downie critiqued and reconstructed the philosophy of palliative care, offering insights into its ethical and practical dimensions, as detailed in their book published by Oxford University Press. 13. Joshi et al. conducted a systematic review on task-shifting for managing non-communicable diseases in lowand middle-income countries, highlighting its potential to address workforce shortages, as published in PLOS One. 14. Ahmed and Jakaria examined the role of community-based skilled birth attendants in Bangladesh, focusing on their contributions to home deliveries, as reported in Reproductive Health Matters. 15. Callaghan et al. reviewed task-shifting for HIV treatment and care in Africa, demonstrating its effectiveness in expanding access to care, as published in Human Resources for Health. 16. Merriman and Harding described the introduction of affordable morphine in Uganda to alleviate end-of-life suffering, showcasing a successful model for pain control in resource-limited settings, as detailed in Philosophy, Ethics, and Humanities in Medicine. 17. The Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD) and the European Union emphasized the importance of strengthening primary care systems to improve health outcomes, as outlined in their report, Health at a Glance: Europe 2016. 18. The WHO Model List of Essential Medicines provides guidance on ensuring the availability of critical medications, including those for palliative care, to address global health needs. 19. Dowell et al. published the CDC guidelines for prescribing opioids for chronic pain in the United States, aiming to balance pain management with the prevention of opioid misuse, as detailed in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report. 20. Joranson et al. 21. Belkin et al. proposed the 5×5 model for scaling up community mental health care in low-income regions, focusing on practical implementation strategies, as published in Psychiatric Services. 22. Patel authored a manual titled Where There Is No Psychiatrist, providing guidance on delivering mental health care in resource-limited settings. 23. Rahman et al. evaluated the impact of a multicomponent behavioral intervention for adults experiencing psychological distress in conflict-affected areas of Pakistan. Their randomized clinical trial demonstrated significant benefits, as published in JAMA. 24. Weobong et al. assessed the long-term effectiveness and cost-efficiency of the Healthy Activity Programme, a brief psychological treatment for depression delivered by lay counselors in primary care, as reported in PLOS Medicine. 25. Hudson et al. developed guidelines for providing psychosocial and bereavement support to family caregivers of palliative care patients, as published in the Journal of Palliative Medicine. 26. Sepulveda et al. outlined the WHO's global perspective on palliative care, emphasizing its integration into health systems worldwide, as detailed in the Journal of Pain and Symptom Management. 27. Stjernswärd et al. proposed a public health strategy for palliative care, highlighting its role in addressing global health inequities, as published in the Journal of Pain and Symptom Management. 28. Kellehear discussed the intersection of health promotion and palliative care, advocating for a patient-centered approach, as featured in the book Palliative Care: A Patient-Centered Approach. 29. Binagwaho et al. reviewed Rwanda's health investments over 20 years, demonstrating significant improvements in health outcomes, as reported in The Lancet. 30. Kurfi et al. identified barriers to primary health care utilization in low-income settings in Nigeria, emphasizing the need for targeted interventions, as published in The Lancet. 31. Thayyil and Cherumanalil assessed the status of patients receiving palliative home care in rural Kerala, India, highlighting the services provided and areas for improvement, as reported in the Indian Journal of Palliative Care. 32. Peterson commented on the Institute of Medicine's report on manpower policy for primary health care, emphasizing the need for strategic workforce planning, as published in Annals of Internal Medicine. 33. Chino et al. examined the financial burden of cancer care, including out-of-pocket costs and underinsurance, and its impact on patients, as reported in JAMA Oncology. 34. Murray et al. conducted qualitative studies on the experiences of patients dying from cancer in developed and developing countries, identifying lessons for improving end-of-life care, as published in BMJ. 35. Beernaert et al. explored barriers and facilitators to early identification of palliative care needs by family physicians, community nurses, and patients, as reported in Palliative Medicine. 36. Williams et al. analyzed the differential impacts of caregiving across various groups in Canada, focusing on end-of-life, long-term, and short-term care, as published in Community Health and Social Care in the Community. 37. The Alma-Ata Declaration of 1978 reaffirmed health as a fundamental human right and emphasized the importance of primary health care in achieving health equity and social justice globally.
